Philex Mining Corporation.desc: Philippine mining company, incorporated in 1955, that explores for and mines gold, copper and silver. It is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange under the ticker PX and had 2,590 employees.

sources.title: Philex Mining Corporation (PSE:PX) - Company Profile
Corporate Profile

Syrah Resources.desc: Australian mining company founded in 2007 and listed on the Australian Securities Exchange under the ticker SYR. It mines graphite and vanadium and runs an anode material plant at Vidalia in the United States; revenue was US$33.4 million in 2025 and it had 374 employees.

sources.title: Syrah Resources Limited (ASX:SYR)

Petra Diamonds.desc: Diamond mining company with a premium listing on the main market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker PDL. It runs three underground mines in South Africa and one open pit in Tanzania, and sold 3.16 million carats of rough diamonds for revenue of US$367 million in the year to 30 June 2024.

sources.title: Audited Full Year 2024 results

South32.desc: Diversified mining and metals company formed in May 2015, with shares listed on the Australian, London and Johannesburg stock exchanges. It produces bauxite, alumina, aluminium, copper, zinc, lead, silver, nickel and manganese ore, and had 8,892 employees in the year to June 2025.

sources.title: South32 Annual Report 2025

Tozzi Green.desc: Italian company working in agriculture and renewable energy. It is part of the Tozzi Holding group, within its Tozzi Renewable Energy branch.

sources.title: Tozzi Green Madagascar (company website, archived copy)

Tozzi Green.note: The only page found describing the firm itself is an archived copy of its own Madagascar website from 2012-13, which gives no revenue, staff or current farmed area. Current Tozzi group pages did not open; the Ravenna headquarters on the card is not confirmed by any page opened.

Tiomin Resources.desc: Canadian mineral exploration company that traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange as TIO and held the Kwale titanium project in Kenya and a half interest in the Pukaqaqa copper-gold deposit in Peru. Shareholders voted on 15 March 2010 to rename it Vaaldiam Mining Inc (TSX: VAA) after it acquired Vaaldiam Resources.

sources.title: MERGER: Tiomin to acquire Vaaldiam
Tiomin Resources Inc. Shareholders Approve Acquisition of Vaaldiam

Samherji.desc: Icelandic seafood company based in Akureyri that fishes with seven vessels, processes whitefish, farms fish on land and sells through its arm Ice Fresh Seafood. Group revenue was 542 million euros in 2025 and it had 832 staff at the end of that year.

sources.title: Strong operations and solid finances at Samherji in 2025

Wildlife Works.desc: Company founded in 1997 by Mike Korchinsky that develops forest conservation projects which generate carbon credits under the REDD+ scheme and sells those credits to companies and investors. It has projects in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Colombia and Indonesia as well as Kenya.

sources.title: What We Do

Veolia Environnement.desc: French company that runs water, waste and energy services for cities and industry on five continents. Revenue was 44.7 billion euros in 2024 and it had about 215,000 staff.

sources.title: Multifaceted performance: Veolia exceeds all its 2024 targets

Saipem.desc: Italian engineering and construction company for energy and infrastructure projects, covering offshore and onshore work, offshore drilling, wind and robotics. Revenue was 14.5 billion euros in 2024 and it had more than 30,000 employees worldwide.

sources.title: Saipem at a glance

ČEZ Group.desc: Czech energy group that generates, distributes and sells electricity, with more than 33,000 direct employees and about 3.5 million customers. Its shares trade on the Prague and Warsaw stock exchanges, and the Czech Republic, through the Ministry of Finance, held 69.78 percent of its share capital at 31 December 2025.

sources.title: About us
Structure of shareholders

Zijin Mining.desc: Chinese mining group incorporated in Fujian Province in September 2000, with its legal address in Shanghang County, that mines copper, gold, zinc, lithium, silver and molybdenum. It is listed in Hong Kong (02899) and Shanghai (601899), and in 2024 reported operating income of about 303.6 billion yuan, 1.07 million tonnes of mined copper and 73 tonnes of mined gold.

sources.title: Zijin Mining Group Annual Report 2024

Shanghai Electric Group.desc: Chinese maker of energy and industrial equipment, including nuclear, coal-fired, wind and energy storage equipment, elevators and electric motors, with headquarters in Changning District, Shanghai. Its shares are listed in Hong Kong (02727) and Shanghai, its parent is the state-owned Shanghai Electric Holding Group, and 2024 revenue was 116.2 billion yuan.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Report
sources.publisher: Shanghai Electric Group Company Limited / HKEXnews

PowerChina.desc: Chinese engineering and construction group founded in September 2011 that does planning, design, building and equipment installation for hydropower, thermal power, renewable energy and other infrastructure, and also works in real estate and finance. Its listed arm trades on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601669) with revenue of 645.6 billion yuan in 2025 and 161,478 employees.

sources.title: The Power Construction Corporation of China
sources.publisher: Belt and Road Portal (yidaiyilu.gov.cn), sourced from sasac.gov.cn

sources.title: Power Construction Corporation of China, Ltd (SHA: 601669) Revenue

Trans Adriatic Pipeline AG.desc: Pipeline company that owns and runs the 877 km Trans Adriatic Pipeline, which carries Azerbaijani gas from the Turkish border across northern Greece and Albania and under the Adriatic Sea to southern Italy. Commercial operations began on 15 November 2020, and by 2025 it had shipped more than 52 billion cubic metres of gas to Europe.

sources.title: TAP marks five years of safe and reliable operations

Tengizchevroil.desc: Kazakhstani partnership that operates the Tengiz oil field in western Kazakhstan. It is held by Chevron (50 percent), ExxonMobil (25 percent), the state company KazMunayGas (20 percent) and Lukoil (5 percent), and a third processing plant started up in January 2025 to take field output towards one million barrels of oil equivalent a day.

sources.title: Chevron Achieves First Oil at Future Growth Project in Kazakhstan

Union Development Group Co., Ltd. (UDG).desc: Property developer that the US Treasury describes as a Chinese state-owned entity. Treasury says it first registered as a Cambodian-owned company with a Cambodian national as its head and reverted to Chinese ownership within three years, and it was placed under US sanctions on 15 September 2020.

sources.title: Treasury Sanctions Chinese State-Owned Entity for Its Role in Corrupt Practices in Cambodia

PT PLN.desc: Indonesia's state electricity company, which generates, transmits, distributes and sells power nationwide and reports to the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises. Revenue was 545.4 trillion rupiah in 2024, of which 353.17 trillion came from electricity sales, and net profit was 17.76 trillion rupiah.

sources.title: Pendapatan PLN meningkat 11,9% jadi Rp 545 triliun sepanjang tahun 2024

PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia (Lonsum).desc: Indonesian plantation company started in 1906 that grows and processes oil palm, rubber, cocoa and tea and sells oil palm seed. At the end of 2024 it had 111,367 hectares of its own planted area and 12 palm oil mills; it has been listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange since 1996 and is controlled by Indofood Agri Resources through PT Salim Ivomas Pratama.

sources.title: Company at a Glance
sources.publisher: PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk

SKS Microfinance.desc: Indian microfinance lender that was renamed Bharat Financial Inclusion Limited and had 8.8 million microfinance customers. It was merged into IndusInd Bank with effect from 4 July 2019 and no longer exists as a separate company.

sources.title: Press release on the merger of Bharat Financial Inclusion Limited with IndusInd Bank
sources.publisher: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) filing

RATCH (Ratchaburi Electricity Generating.desc: Thai investment holding company in power generation and infrastructure, founded on 7 March 2000 and now named RATCH Group. It is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand as RATCH, its largest shareholder is the state Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand with 45 percent, and its equity-share generating capacity was 9,484 MW as of 1 April 2026.

sources.title: Company Background

WTK Holdings.desc: Malaysian group whose main business is logging, with eight timber concessions covering about 402,000 hectares in Sarawak, plus oil palm plantation and food businesses. In the year to December 2024 its timber segment had revenue of RM203.9 million, its plantation segment RM295.3 million and its food segment RM103.7 million, and a subsidiary stopped plywood making in Bintulu on 1 January 2025.

sources.title: WTK exits loss-making plywood manufacturing ops

Shin Yang Group.desc: Malaysian group based in Miri, Sarawak, with timber and shipping businesses. In the year to June 2009 it reported revenue of RM673.5 million, and it owned seven plywood mills in Bintulu and Miri and a fleet of 238 vessels through its shipping arm, Shin Yang Shipping Corporation Berhad, which listed on Bursa Malaysia in 2010.

sources.title: Shin Yang likely to list its timber operations next

Proman.desc: Privately held company headquartered in Switzerland that turns natural gas into chemicals and fertilisers, with combined installed capacity of more than 10 million tonnes a year of methanol, anhydrous ammonia, UAN and melamine. Its plants are in Trinidad and Tobago, the United States and Oman, and it also produces natural gas, builds plants and runs shipping and power businesses.

sources.title: Who we are
What we do

WWF.desc: Network of independently incorporated conservation organisations that has worked since 1961 and has offices in more than 50 countries and projects in over 100. Network services are provided by WWF-International near Geneva, Switzerland; the largest member, the US nonprofit World Wildlife Fund, Inc., had operating revenue of US$486 million in the year to 30 June 2024.

sources.title: World Wildlife Fund, Inc. Consolidated Financial Statements, year ended 30 June 2024

Twigg Exploration and Mining Limitada.desc: Mozambican graphite mining company, wholly owned by the Australian-listed Syrah Resources. In 2023 it was approved for a loan of up to US$150 million from the US International Development Finance Corporation towards a US$175 million expansion to produce up to 350,000 tonnes of graphite a year.

sources.title: Twigg Exploration and Mining Ltda. (DFC-2023-TWIGGEXPLORATI)

Société Minière de Dinguiraye (SMD).desc: Guinean gold mining company and a subsidiary of the Nordgold group. It reported paying 326.5 billion Guinean francs in taxes for 2021 and 31.7 billion francs into the FODEL local development fund in March 2022.

sources.title: La SMD-Nordgold, une entreprise citoyenne au coeur du développement en Guinée (paid advertorial)

PT Harapan Sawit Lestari (PT HSL).desc: Indonesian oil palm plantation and palm oil milling company in Manis Mata, Ketapang district, West Kalimantan, registered as a foreign investment and listed as a subsidiary of Cargill Incorporated. Its land title covers about 5,137 hectares, and its filings describe a further 3,884 hectares of new planting split between its own estate and smallholders.

sources.title: Summary report of planning and management, PT Harapan Sawit Lestari

PT Permata Hijau Pasaman I.desc: Oil palm plantation company in Pasaman Barat district, West Sumatra, Indonesia. Certification filings name PT Permata Hijau Pasaman as a subsidiary of the Singapore-listed Wilmar International Limited, and its estates feed a mill run with the neighbouring Wilmar company PT Gersindo Minang Plantation.

sources.title: Notification of RSPO ASA 1.4: PT Gersindo Minang Plantation and PT Permata Hijau Pasaman, subsidiary of Wilmar International Ltd

Wuzhishan L.S. Group.desc: Company registered in Phnom Penh as Wuzhishan L.S Group Co., Ltd, with an address on Street 55 in Khan Daun Penh. On 30 December 2005 it signed a 70-year Cambodian concession agreement for 10,000 hectares, part of a 20,500-hectare area in Mondulkiri, to plant pine, vegetables and fruit trees and to tap resin and cut timber.

sources.title: Contract for pine plantation between the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and Wuzhishan L.S Group Co., Ltd

Sabi Star / Max Mind Investments.desc: Max Mind Investments (Zimbabwe) Private Limited is a lithium mining company holding the Sabi Star project in Buhera district, Manicaland, with open-pit workings over about 3,800 hectares and an estimated resource of about 5 million tonnes of lithium-tantalum ore. China's Chengxin Lithium Group, listed in Shenzhen, bought a 51 percent stake in November 2021 for about US$76.5 million.

sources.title: Sabi Star Lithium Mine
sources.publisher: Africa Mining Tracker, China Global South Project

PT Mikgro Metal Perdana (MMP).desc: Indonesian iron ore mining company, a joint venture between PT Allindo Indonesia and Aempire Resource Ltd of China, holding a production permit over about 2,000 hectares on Bangka Island, North Minahasa, North Sulawesi. Indonesia's Supreme Court cancelled that permit in August 2016.

sources.title: MEMR tells Mikgro to relocate iron ore mine in N. Sulawesi

Rui Feng (Cambodia) International Co. Lt.desc: Chinese-owned sugar company in Cambodia, one of a set of firms linked to Hengfu Group Sugar Industry Co., Ltd. of Guangdong province. It was granted a 9,000-hectare economic land concession in Preah Vihear in 2011, later cut by 1,000 hectares, and built a US$360 million mill and refinery on a 215-hectare site that can process 20,000 tonnes of cane into 2,000 tonnes of refined sugar a day and employs about 1,000 people.

sources.title: Sugarcane in Preah Vihear (China in Cambodia special report)

Shanghai Xinmingyuan Automobile Parts Co.desc: Car parts manufacturer in Shanghai, China.

Shanghai Kangshuo Co Ltd.desc: Shanghai company that recycles used goods and materials, reported under the full name Shanghai Kangshuo Waste Recycling Co.

Roads Department of Georgia.desc: Georgian government body under the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure, based at 12 Al. Kazbegi Avenue in Tbilisi. It designs, builds, rebuilds and maintains Georgia's international and intrastate roads, monitors road protection rules and can restrict traffic in agreement with the Patrol Police.

Sakhalin Energy (Shell 55%, Mitsui 25%,.desc: Company set up to develop the Sakhalin-2 oil and gas project in Russia's Far East, including a liquefied natural gas plant with capacity of 9.6 million tonnes a year. Gazprom bought a half-share plus one share for US$7.45 billion in cash, leaving Shell with about 27.5 percent, Mitsui 12.5 percent and Mitsubishi 10 percent.

sources.title: Gazprom acquires controlling stake in Sakhalin-2

PT Intraco Penta.desc: Indonesian distributor of heavy equipment and spare parts, founded in 1970 and listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as INTA. It also rents and repairs machinery and does mining contracting; revenue was 966.9 billion rupiah in 2025, with a loss of 69.5 billion rupiah, and it had 496 employees.

sources.title: PT Intraco Penta Tbk (IDX:INTA)

Sarawak Oil Palms.desc: Malaysian oil palm company founded in 1968 and based in Miri, Sarawak, listed on Bursa Malaysia as SOP. It grows, mills, refines and trades palm products and also has a property development arm, with 7,513 employees.

sources.title: Sarawak Oil Palms Berhad (KLSE:SOP) - Company Profile

Yakjin.desc: South Korean garment maker, Yakjin Trading Corporation, founded in 1978 and based in Seoul. It supplies clothing to retailers including Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy, JCPenney and Walmart from eight large factories in Southeast Asia: five in Vietnam, two in Cambodia and one in Indonesia.

sources.title: Yakjin Ho Chi Minh Company Limited - company profile

Vedan Enterprise Corp / Vedan Vietnam.desc: Vedan Enterprise Corporation is a Taiwanese food and seasoning company based in Shalu District, Taichung, which began making monosodium glutamate in 1954 and took its present name in 1972; a related company, Vedan International (Holdings) Limited, listed in Hong Kong in 2003. Its Vietnamese arm, set up in 1991 with a factory in Dong Nai province, makes MSG, starch, glucose syrup, lysine and chlor-alkali, had 3,719 staff at the end of June 2024 and took US$79.5 million of revenue in Vietnam in the first half of 2024.

MSG maker Vedan Vietnam earns $79.5 mln in H1, down 3.4%

Tunas Baru Lampung (TBLA).desc: Indonesian agribusiness that makes vegetable cooking oil from its own oil palm plantations in Lampung and controls a land bank of more than 60,000 hectares. It is part of the Sungai Budi Group, has been listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as TBLA since 14 February 2000, and its two largest shareholders are Budi Delta Swakarya (30.05 percent) and Sungai Budi (28.63 percent).

sources.title: Tunas Baru Lampung - Indonesian company profile

Shell Brasil (Shell group).desc: Shell Brasil Petróleo Ltda is the Brazilian arm of Shell plc and holds stakes in Brazil's pre-salt offshore oil projects, including the Atapu and Mero fields.

sources.title: Shell grows interest in Atapu and Mero units offshore Brazil

PT Bio Inti Agrindo.desc: Indonesian oil palm plantation company in Merauke Regency, Papua, holding land use rights over 34,195 hectares with 21,166 hectares planted as of December 2022 and three crude palm oil mills. Daewoo International Corporation bought 85 percent of it in 2011; POSCO held 60.3 percent of Daewoo in 2013.

Wintek.desc: Taiwanese maker of touch screens, based in Greater Taichung and publicly traded in Taipei, which supplied Apple. It lost NT$15.03 billion over the three years to 2013 and NT$3.42 billion in the first half of 2014, then cut costs from September 2014 by closing three plants in China and a TFT-LCD plant in Taoyuan, laying off 2,360 staff in Taiwan with about 4,300 cuts in all, and moving towards LED lighting and food biotechnology.

Apple Touch Screen Supplier Wintek Restructures to Become New LED Player

Thor Chemical Holdings / Guernica.desc: Thor Chemicals ran a mercury recovery factory at Cato Ridge in KwaZulu-Natal that took in mercury-bearing waste from chemical companies in South Africa and abroad; the government closed it in 1991 and the Thor group then demerged. Guernica Chemicals Limited is a South African company that the UK-based Tato Holdings, described as the restructured former parent of the South African Thor company, approached in 2019 about the Cato Ridge site.

PowerChina Resources / Sinohydro.desc: Sinohydro Corporation Limited is a Chinese builder of dams and hydropower schemes, dating from the early 1950s, with offices in Beijing and work also in power, transport, civil works, mining and real estate; it reports more than 10,000 employees and 524 international projects in over 74 countries worth nearly US$42.5 billion. It is a brand of the state engineering group PowerChina, which was formed in September 2011.

Rimbunan Hijau.desc: Malaysian family group founded in 1975 by Tiong Hiew King and his brothers, who came from Sibu, Sarawak, starting in hardware and building materials. It now works in timber, oil palm, hotels, retail, media, information technology and finance across Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Russia and China; its media arm Media Chinese International publishes four dailies that account for 70 percent of Malaysia's Chinese-language newspaper business, and Forbes put the Tiong family's wealth at US$820 million. Tiong Hiew King, the group's executive chairman, died in November 2025.

sources.title: Sarawak timber tycoon Tiong Hiew King laid to rest

WTK Group.desc: Sarawak-based Malaysian group whose businesses span logging, oil palm, property, manufacturing, hotels and shipping. Its main listed company is WTK Holdings Berhad, whose managing director is Patrick Haw Yeong and whose substantial shareholders include Kie Yik Wong and the family-held WTK Realty Sdn Bhd. More than 30 companies registered in Papua New Guinea are linked to the group through shared directors and shareholders; 12 concessions tied to it exported about 1.3 million cubic metres of logs between 2019 and 2021, 14 percent of all PNG log exports.

sources.title: PNG's Timber Barons: #1 - The WTK Cluster
